description: Live steering from the user: a far-grabbed object (pan) has only two states, very far when grabbed and glued to the hand as soon as S is pressed in the XR Device Simulator. They want: while S is held the object moves slowly closer, and when S is released it stays at that distance (so the pan can be placed on the stove easily). Root cause found in the XRI source (Library/PackageCache/com.unity.xr.interaction.toolkit@8a8cfde33e41/Runtime/Interaction/Attachment/InteractionAttachController.cs, see context.json grab_distance_findings): the rig's NearFarInteractor creates a default InteractionAttachController at runtime (nothing serialized in the XR Origin prefab) with distance-based velocity scaling and momentum ON; pulling the hand back (S moves the simulated controller back) is amplified by (1 + movementScale) where movementScale reaches maxAdditionalVelocityScalar(1.5) * pivot(distance), momentum keeps pulling after the key is released, and when the offset reaches ~0 the attach snaps into the hand (ResetOffset). Independent of FEAT-002/003 (no shared files), run after them.
steps: Create Assets/Scripts/Common/GrabDistanceTuning.cs (+ .cs.meta, fresh guid, MonoImporter format like Assets/Scripts/Cooking/PanSnap.cs.meta). Global namespace like HeldObjectPhysics. `public static class GrabDistanceTuning` (or a small class with a static installer) in the style of HeldObjectPhysics: `[RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(RuntimeInitializeLoadType.AfterSceneLoad)]` installer that subscribes SceneManager.sceneLoaded (unsubscribe first, stays safe with Domain Reload disabled) and calls `public static int ApplyAll()` which uses Object.FindObjectsByType<InteractionAttachController>(FindObjectsInactive.Include, FindObjectsSortMode.None) (namespace UnityEngine.XR.Interaction.Toolkit.Attachment) and calls `public static void Apply(InteractionAttachController c)`. Constants (public const or static readonly, documented): useMomentum = false (nothing keeps moving after the key is released); zVelocityRampThreshold = 0 (so a slow 0.2 m/s keyboard pull is not attenuated by the ramp factor); minAdditionalVelocityScalar = 0; maxAdditionalVelocityScalar = 0.3 (distance amplification stays gentle: at most about 1.9x at 3 m instead of up to 5.5x); keep useDistanceBasedVelocityScaling true (so hand motion still reaches further than the arm) unless the XRI source reading shows the pull is impossible without it. Verify by reading ComputeAmplifiedOffset in InteractionAttachController.cs that these values make the pull speed roughly equal to the hand speed times (1 + 0.3 * distance) at most, and write that derivation in a class XML doc. Also set manipulationTranslateSpeed to a gentle value (0.4) in case the thumbstick manipulation input is enabled later (useManipulationInput is false by default, leave it as is). Setting minAdditionalVelocityScalar/maxAdditionalVelocityScalar: note the setters clamp (max 0..5) and OnValidate orders min/max, set min first.

Make the installer idempotent and cheap (runs once per scene load), and also cover the case where the NearFarInteractor creates the controller late: in Apply nothing else is needed, but add a second hook so a controller added later is also tuned: e.g. a tiny internal MonoBehaviour `GrabDistanceTuningMarker` is NOT wanted; instead re-run ApplyAll once from a coroutine-free place such as the first call after XRInteractionManager registers (keep it simple: ApplyAll at AfterSceneLoad and on sceneLoaded is enough; document the limitation like HeldObjectPhysics does).

Do not edit Assets/Samples/**/XR Origin (XR Rig).prefab, XR Device Simulator prefab or SampleScene.unity. The tuning is runtime-only so the user's rig stays untouched. Expose the constants as public static settable fields or add `[Tooltip]`-documented constants at the top so the user can retune in one place; mention in the class doc that the simulator's own controller Z speed is XRDeviceSimulator keyboardZTranslateSpeed (0.2 m/s in the sample prefab) and is the other knob.

Add EditMode test Assets/Scripts/Tests/EditMode/GrabDistanceTuningTests.cs: Apply on a fresh `new GameObject().AddComponent<InteractionAttachController>()` sets useMomentum false, zVelocityRampThreshold 0, min/max scalars as specified (Destroy with DestroyImmediate in teardown). Test fails if Apply is removed or constants change inconsistently.

Add PlayMode test Assets/Scripts/Tests/PlayMode/GrabDistanceTuningPlayTests.cs that drives the real controller deterministically through the IInteractionAttachController interface (public: GetOrCreateAnchorTransform(), MoveTo(Vector3), DoUpdate(float), hasOffset): create an XROrigin object (Unity.XR.CoreUtils, with Origin/Camera child as needed, see HeldObjectPhysicsTests.MakeRig), a 'follow' Transform, an InteractionAttachController with transformToFollow = follow and motionStabilizationMode = Never; get the anchor, MoveTo a point 3 m in front of follow; then for 50 steps of 0.02 s move `follow` backwards (toward the player, along the anchor offset axis) at 0.2 m/s and call DoUpdate(0.02f), then stop moving and call DoUpdate 100 more times. Assert for the TUNED controller (Apply called): (a) after the pull the distance anchor-to-follow is smaller than at the start but not collapsed to the hand, and the closing speed during the pull stays below 1.0 m/s on average; (b) once the follow stops, the offset does not change any more (no momentum, difference < 1 mm over the 100 steps). Also assert the DEFAULT (untuned) controller either keeps drifting after stopping or closes faster than the tuned one, so the test proves the tuning changes behavior (if the default does not differ in this harness, drop that comparison and keep (a) and (b)). If driving DoUpdate needs the XR Origin lookup (ComponentLocatorUtility<XROrigin>), make sure the origin exists before the controller's OnEnable (create the controller GameObject inactive, activate after the rig exists).
Run compile_check.ps1 (runtime + EditMode + PlayMode) and fix every error. Record that the tests could not be run (Unity is open) and list the test names in findings.
acceptance_criteria: GrabDistanceTuning.Apply disables momentum, removes the ramp attenuation and bounds the distance amplification of every InteractionAttachController in the loaded scenes at scene load, without editing any scene or rig prefab
The new EditMode and PlayMode tests exist, compile, and would fail if Apply were removed (settings asserted explicitly, pull/stop behavior asserted numerically)
Class doc explains the cause (amplification + momentum + reset snap) and where to retune
verification: Re-read InteractionAttachController.ComputeAmplifiedOffset against the chosen constants and confirm in findings that the pull speed matches the derivation
findings: Added Assets/Scripts/Common/GrabDistanceTuning.cs (+meta), EditMode GrabDistanceTuningTests.cs and PlayMode GrabDistanceTuningPlayTests.cs (+metas). compile_check.ps1: TOTAL ERRORS: 0. Tests NOT run (Unity Editor open, no batchmode); not committed (git unavailable). EditMode tests: Defaults_DifferFromTuning, Apply_DisablesMomentumAndRamp, Apply_BoundsDistanceAmplification, Apply_IsIdempotent, Apply_NullIsIgnored, ApplyAll_TunesControllersInTheScene. PlayMode tests: Tuned_PullIsSlowAndGentle, Tuned_StaysWhereItIsAfterThePullStops, Tuned_ClosesSlowerThanDefault. Constants: useMomentum false, zVelocityRampThreshold 0, min/max additional scalar 0/0.3, manipulationTranslateSpeed 0.4, distance scaling stays on. Derivation checked against ComputeAmplifiedOffset: movement = zMotion*rampAmount*(1+movementScale)*dt, movementScale <= 0.3*pivot, so pull <= hand speed*(1+0.3*dist) (about 0.38 m/s at 3 m for 0.2 m/s); no momentum so the offset is constant once the hand stops. Snap into hand: ResetOffset is called only when newOffset dot start < 0.05 (offset length <= 0), i.e. only if S is held until the object reaches the hand; the offset is already ~0 then so the jump is at most one frame. Tests drive real frames because AttachPointVelocityTracker uses Time.unscaledTime; XROrigin needs Origin and Camera set (tracker dereferences Camera). MotionStabilizationMode is a top-level enum in the Attachment namespace. Run compile_check.ps1 with -ExecutionPolicy Bypass.
